basic_information.short_title: Salamat Excellence Award for Leadership Act of 2025
basic_information.official_title: AN ACT ESTABLISHING AND INSTITUTIONALIZING THE SALAMAT EXCELLENCE AWARD FOR LEADERSHIP PROGRAM FOR THE BANGSAMORO AUTONOMOUS REGION IN MUSLIM MINDANAO, AND ALLOCATING FOR THIS PURPOSE THE SALAMAT EXCELLENCE AWARD FOR LEADERSHIP ENDOWMENT FUND
basic_information.effectivity: 15 days after complete publication in the Bangsamoro Gazette or a newspaper of regional circulation, whichever is earlier

citizen_summary.what_is_this_about: Creates an annual leadership award for one leader in the region, backed by a ₱500 million endowment fund invested under Islamic financing principles — with the winner's LGU or organisation receiving a ₱20 million development grant.
citizen_summary.why_was_it_proposed: The interior ministry already ran a SEAL programme administratively. This gives it a statute, a three-stage assessment process with named committees, and — the substantive change — a permanent endowment so the award does not depend on an annual budget line.
citizen_summary.what_will_change: One awardee is chosen each year through three levels of assessment, by a Selection Committee chaired by the Senior Minister and seating the Grand Mufti, voting in secret. The awardee receives a ₱500,000 medallion; their LGU, organisation or institution receives ₱20 million that may only be spent on development projects. The endowment's principal stays invested; only its returns pay out.
who_will_be_affected: Leaders in the BARMM eligible for nomination — local officials and leaders of organisations and institutions
The LGU, organisation or institution the awardee represents, which receives the grant
Higher education institutions in the region, which must integrate awardees' leadership models into public administration courses
The Bangsamoro Treasury Office, which manages the fund as trustee
Civil society, health, women, youth, business, religious, indigenous peoples and disability sectors, all represented on the Validation Team
citizen_summary.when_will_it_take_effect: In force since 2025 — approved by the Chief Minister on 24 September 2025, effective 15 days after publication. Implementing rules were due within 45 days of effectivity.

what_this_means_for_you.in_short: NOW LAW. If you lead an LGU or an organisation in the region, you can be nominated for this — one award a year, and the ₱20 million that comes with it goes to your LGU or organisation for development projects, not to you.
in_practice: One SEAL awardee per year, selected by secret vote
Three leadership domains assessed: accountable, participatory and service-oriented leadership
Three levels of assessment — screening by a technical working group, onsite validation by a Validation Team, and final interviews by a Selection Committee
You must score at least 75% in each domain and 80% overall at the second level to reach the shortlist
You must have no pending civil, criminal or administrative case, and never have won before
Their LGU, organisation or institution receives a ₱20,000,000 grant
₱500,000,000 seeds a permanent endowment fund, invested as far as practicable in Shari'ah-compliant products
If nobody qualifies in a given year, no award is given and the money rolls over

for_specific_groups.Local chief executives: You are the most obvious nominees, and the grant your LGU receives is governed by the same rules as the 20% of the National Tax Allotment reserved for local development projects.
for_specific_groups.Organisations and institutions: A leader representing you may be nominated, and any incentive must be used only to further your primary purpose.
for_specific_groups.Applicants generally: Applications go to the MILG Provincial Focal Person, who endorses them to the regional office. The ministry sets the documentary requirements.
for_specific_groups.Higher education institutions: Documented information, case studies and leadership models from awardees must be institutionalised in your public administration courses, subject to Commission on Higher Education guidelines.
for_specific_groups.Academics: The ministry engages accredited academic institutions in documentation, assessment and validation, with honoraria payable from the programme's appropriation.
for_specific_groups.Sectoral representatives: Civil society, health, women, youth, business, religious, indigenous peoples and persons with disability each hold two Validation Team seats.

what_this_means_for_you.when_you_will_feel_it: In force since 2025. The existing MILG programme transitioned into the statutory one on effectivity.
what_you_can_do: Submit an application to the MILG Provincial Focal Person, who endorses it to the regional office
Check the eligibility bar first — no pending civil, criminal or administrative case, and no prior conferment
Note the interpretive rule: the burden is on you to show you qualify, and the criteria are construed strictly against you
If your LGU wins, the grant may only fund development projects — not salaries, vehicles, offices, travel or administrative costs
watch_out_for: ₱500 million is committed as endowment principal for an awards programme. For comparison, the Ancestral Domain Fund under BAA 64 received ₱200 million, the Transitional Justice Commission ₱150 million, the whole Internally Displaced Persons programme ₱50 million, and the entire Labor and Employment Code ₱30 million.

Section 12 contradicts itself on scoring. The text says the Third Level Assessment contributes 40% of the overall rating; the formula printed immediately below it reads 10% + 60% + 30%. Only the formula sums to 100.
Section 22 requires all criteria and rules to be strictly construed against the nominee, with the burden on the nominee to show they qualify — an unusually adverse canon for an award.
Only one award may be given each year, and no person may win twice.
The Selection Committee declares awardees by secret voting, and the act sets out no publication requirement for the reasons.
The act nowhere explains whom or what the award is named for.

key_terms_explained.SEAL: Salamat Excellence Award for Leadership — described in the act as the highest leadership award, incentive, honour and recognition-based programme for all leaders in the BARMM.
key_terms_explained.Endowment fund: A permanent capital fund. The principal stays invested and only the returns are spent, so the award does not depend on a yearly appropriation.
key_terms_explained.Vicegerency: Khalifa — the Islamic concept of humanity holding authority as a trust, answerable for how it is exercised. Listed among the principles of accountable leadership.
key_terms_explained.Shari'ah-compliant investment: Investment products conforming to Islamic finance principles, which prohibit interest and certain speculative or prohibited activities.
key_terms_explained.National Tax Allotment: The share of national taxes given to LGUs, 20% of which is reserved for local development projects. The grant is governed by those same rules.
key_terms_explained.Darul-Ifta': The regional office of Islamic legal opinion. Its Grand Mufti sits on the Selection Committee.
key_terms_explained.Validation Team: The body conducting onsite second-level verification of a candidate's claims, through document review, site visits and community interviews.

what_this_means_for_you.status_note: Passed 20 August 2025 and approved by the Chief Minister on 24 September 2025.

benefits.headline: A permanently endowed leadership award — ₱500,000 to the leader, ₱20 million in development money to the community they lead.

direct_benefits.how_to_access: Section 14, after passing all three assessment levels and ranking first

direct_benefits.benefit: A ₱20,000,000 grant to the awardee's LGU, organisation or institution
direct_benefits.who_gets_it: The community or body the awardee represents
direct_benefits.how_to_access: Section 14, released from the endowment's profits on the Selection Committee's certification

direct_benefits.benefit: A permanent endowment so the award does not depend on the annual budget
direct_benefits.who_gets_it: The programme itself, and future awardees
direct_benefits.how_to_access: Section 15 — ₱500,000,000 seed capital held in trust by the Bangsamoro Treasury Office

direct_benefits.benefit: Sectoral seats on the body that validates candidates onsite
direct_benefits.who_gets_it: Civil society, health, women, youth, business, religious, indigenous peoples and disability sectors

direct_benefits.benefit: Honoraria for academic participants in assessment and validation

indirect_benefits: Documented leadership models taught in public administration courses across the region's higher education institutions
An annual analytical report from the academe on best practices and lessons learned
Onsite validation with community interviews, rather than assessment on paper alone
Investment of public capital under Islamic financing principles
limitations: One awardee a year, from the whole region.
The grant is restricted to development projects and may not fund operations.
The interpretive rule runs against the nominee.
Where no candidate qualifies, no award is made.

for_nominees: Meet the eligibility bar: good moral character, no pending civil, criminal or administrative case, no adverse judgment, and no previous conferment
Submit the documentary requirements the interior ministry sets
Carry the burden of showing that you qualify — the criteria and rules are strictly construed against you
for_awardee_recipients: Spend the grant only on development projects under the rules governing the 20% local development share, the Annual Investment Program and the Local Development Investment Program
If an organisation, spend it only to further your primary purpose

Do not use it for micro credits or loans, travel outside the Act's purposes, administrative expenses, cash gifts, bonuses, allowances, uniforms, utilities, vehicles not directly used for the undertaking, salaries or per diems, office construction or refurbishing, or loan guarantees
for_government: MILG hosts the technical working group, sets documentary requirements, engages the academe and organises the awarding ceremony
The Bangsamoro Treasury Office manages the endowment as trustee, determines the investment strategy, and withdraws only on the Selection Committee's certification
MILG and the finance ministry jointly issue implementing rules within 45 days of effectivity

what_is_prohibited: Using the incentive for micro credits and loans.
Using it for travel, domestic or foreign, except in advancement of the Act's purposes.
Using it for administrative expenses, including cash gifts, bonuses, food allowances, staff uniforms, communication bills, utilities and transportation costs.
Purchasing, maintaining or repairing motor vehicles or motorcycles not directly used for the SEAL undertaking.
Paying salaries, wages, emoluments, per diems or overtime.
Constructing, repairing or refurnishing administrative offices.
Using it as a loan guarantee.
Withdrawing from the endowment fund without a Selection Committee certification naming the awardee and authorising the withdrawal.

penalties.for_citizens: None. The act creates no offence, fine or imprisonment.
penalties.eligibility_bar: A nominee with any pending civil, criminal or administrative case, or any adverse judgment, is disqualified — as is anyone previously conferred with the award.
penalties.interpretive_rule: Section 22 requires all definitions of the criteria and all rules issued under the Act to be strictly construed against the leader-nominee, who bears the burden of showing they qualify.

where_to_complain.first_stop: The MILG Provincial Focal Person, who receives applications and endorses them to the regional office
where_to_complain.oversight: The Technical Working Group within MILG's Operations Management Service; the Validation Team; and the Selection Committee chaired by the Senior Minister of the Office of the Chief Minister
where_to_complain.note: The act creates no appeal or protest mechanism against a selection decision.

everyday_scenarios: A municipality's mayor is nominated for consistently transparent budgeting. The Validation Team conducts an onsite visit and interviews the community before any shortlisting.
A winning LGU wants to use the ₱20 million for staff bonuses. It cannot — Section 16 bars salaries, bonuses, allowances and administrative expenses, and confines the money to development projects.
No candidate clears the third-level assessment in a given year. Section 13 declares no awardee and retains the award fund for the next cycle, or lets the treasury invest it.
A public administration student in the region studies a case on a past awardee. Section 20 requires awardees' documented leadership models to be built into those courses.

key_provisions: Sections 1–3 — Short title: “The Salamat Excellence Award for Leadership Act of 2025”. Policy: recognise and institutionalise exemplary leadership embodying moral governance, accountability and inclusive development, honouring leaders who exemplify the Bangsamoro's aspirations for self-determination, peace and progress. SEAL is described as the highest leadership award, incentive, honour and recognition-based programme for all leaders in the BARMM, assessed across three domains — Accountable Leadership, guided by transparency, honesty, accountability, integrity, vicegerency, flexibility, moderation and righteousness; Participatory Leadership, guided by participation, justness, fairness and equity, consultation, consensus building, inclusiveness and gender sensitivity; and Service-Oriented Leadership, guided by efficiency, effectiveness, general welfare, responsiveness, justice, fairness and equity.

Sections 4–5 — Definitions of the three assessment levels and the bodies conducting them. A Technical Working Group is created within the Ministry of the Interior and Local Government under its Operations Management Service to implement the programme: producing information materials, drafting and revising the tools and criteria, receiving applications through a Provincial Focal Person for endorsement to the regional office, reviewing documents, conducting the First Level Assessment, convening the Validation Team and Selection Committee, maintaining a database of assessment results, preparing a terminal report, and organising the awarding ceremony.

Sections 6–7 — The Validation Team is chaired by the MILG Director II for Operations Management Services, with technical representatives from ministries at Division Chief rank or above, the MILG Focal Person for the Search for Model Barangay, the Dean of the College of Public Affairs–Public Administration of Mindanao State University Main Campus, two representatives each from civil society organisations, the health sector, the women sector, the youth sector, the business sector, the religious sector, indigenous peoples' affairs and persons with disability, and one from the academe. It reviews applications, conducts the Second Level Assessment through onsite visits and interviews with stakeholders and the community, shortlists qualified candidates, deliberates, and presents its reports to the Selection Committee.

Sections 8–9 — The Selection Committee is chaired by the Senior Minister of the Office of the Chief Minister, co-chaired by the Minister of the Interior and Local Government, with the Bangsamoro Director General of MILG as Vice-Chairperson, and as members the chairperson of Parliament's Committee on Local Governance, the Grand Mufti of the Regional Darul-Ifta', the Mindanao State University dean, one representative from a non-governmental organisation focusing on leadership and governance, one from the Chamber of Commerce, three from civil society organisations or institutions focusing on leadership and governance, and the MILG Director II for Operations Management Services. It reviews the validation results, conducts final interviews under the SEAL Leadership Framework, and convenes to “declare the awardees of the SEAL Program through secret voting” — selecting one awardee for the current year.

Sections 10–12 — Eligibility: good moral character; no pending civil, criminal or administrative case; no adverse judgment in any criminal or administrative case; and no previous conferment of the award. The interior ministry sets the documentary requirements. Selection runs through three levels. The First Level Assessment by the technical working group contributes 10% of the final score. The Second Level Assessment is an onsite validation scored against the three leadership domains; to be shortlisted a candidate must score at least 75% in each domain and at least 80% overall, and this level contributes 60%. The Third Level Assessment is the Selection Committee's final interview, with the three domains equally weighted — the text states this contributes 40%, while the formula printed immediately below reads “First Level 10% (10%) + Second Level 60% (60%) + Third Level 30% (30%)”. The highest-rated nominee is selected, with ties resolved by a vote during deliberation.

Sections 13–14 — If no qualified or eligible nominee passes the Third Level Assessment, the Selection Committee declares no awardee for that fiscal year, and the award fund is retained in the Special SEAL Fund for the next cycle or invested by the treasury. The awardee receives a SEAL medallion worth ₱500,000 and a grant of ₱20,000,000 to the local government unit, organisation or institution of the awardee's representation.

Sections 15–18 — A SEAL Endowment Fund is established, managed by the Bangsamoro Treasury Office as trustee, with ₱500,000,000 appropriated as seed capital, and a special account called the Special SEAL Fund serving as depository for the seed capital and realised profits. The Fund is used exclusively to pay the incentives to the awardee and their LGU, organisation or institution. Where the awardee represents an LGU, the incentive is governed by the policies for the 20% of the annual National Tax Allotment reserved for local development projects, the Annual Investment Program and the Local Development Investment Program; where an organisation, only for the furtherance of its primary purpose. The incentives may not be used for micro credits and loans; travel except in advancement of the Act; administrative expenses including cash gifts, bonuses, food allowances, staff uniforms, communication bills, utilities and transportation; motor vehicles not directly used for the undertaking; salaries, wages, emoluments, per diems or overtime; construction, repair or refurnishing of administrative offices; or loan guarantees. The treasury determines the investment strategy and, “as far as practicable”, invests the endowment in Shari'ah-compliant and/or Islamic financing investment products, whether foreign or local. It withdraws only the profits corresponding to the incentives, and only on a Selection Committee certification naming the awardee and authorising the withdrawal.

Sections 19–22 — The interior ministry engages accredited academic institutions within the BARMM in documenting, assessing and validating awardees' leadership exemplars, developing evidence-based evaluation methodologies, conducting independent reviews of documented achievements and governance innovations, and submitting an annual analytical report. Documented information, case studies and leadership models from awardees “shall be institutionalized in the Public Administration courses of higher education institutions in BARMM”, subject to Commission on Higher Education guidelines, with impact on leadership education reviewed every 3 years in coordination with Mindanao State University, Cotabato State University and other state and private universities. Academic participants receive honoraria charged against the programme's annual appropriation. In interpreting the Act, “all definitions of the criteria and all rules and regulations issued pursuant to this Act shall be strictly construed against the leader-nominee. It shall be the burden of the leader-nominee to show that it qualifies for the SEAL.”

Sections 23–27 — Implementing rules jointly formulated by MILG and the Ministry of Finance, and Budget and Management within 45 days from effectivity. On effectivity, the existing SEAL Program of the interior ministry transitions into the statutory programme. Separability and repealing clauses. Effective 15 days after complete publication in the Bangsamoro Gazette or a newspaper of regional circulation, whichever is earlier.

citizen_questions.a: Any leader in the BARMM — the act frames it as covering all leaders, and the incentive contemplates awardees representing either a local government unit or an organisation or institution. You must have good moral character, no pending civil, criminal or administrative case, no adverse judgment, and no previous conferment.

citizen_questions.q: What does the winner actually get?
citizen_questions.a: A medallion worth ₱500,000. The ₱20 million goes to the local government unit, organisation or institution the awardee represents — not to the awardee personally — and may only be spent on development projects.

citizen_questions.q: Can the ₱20 million be used for salaries or a new office?
citizen_questions.a: No. Section 16 bars salaries, wages, per diems and overtime; cash gifts, bonuses, allowances, uniforms, utilities and transportation; vehicles not directly used for the undertaking; construction, repair or refurnishing of administrative offices; travel outside the Act's purposes; micro credits and loans; and loan guarantees.

By a ₱500,000,000 endowment fund held in trust by the Bangsamoro Treasury Office. The principal stays invested — as far as practicable in Shari'ah-compliant or Islamic financing products — and only the profits are withdrawn to pay the incentives, on a certification from the Selection Committee.

citizen_questions.q: How many awards are given each year?
citizen_questions.a: One. And if no candidate passes the final assessment, none is given — the money stays in the Special SEAL Fund for the next cycle.
Through three levels — a technical screening, an onsite validation with community interviews, and a final interview by the Selection Committee, which declares the awardee by secret voting.

citizen_questions.q: Who sits on the Selection Committee?
citizen_questions.a: The Senior Minister of the Office of the Chief Minister as chair, the interior Minister as co-chair, the ministry's Director General as vice-chair, and as members the chair of Parliament's Committee on Local Governance, the Grand Mufti of the Regional Darul-Ifta', a Mindanao State University dean, an NGO representative, a Chamber of Commerce representative, three civil society representatives, and a ministry director.

views.simple: Establishes the Salamat Excellence Award for Leadership as a statutory programme: one awardee a year chosen through three levels of assessment by a Selection Committee voting in secret, judged on accountable, participatory and service-oriented leadership; a ₱500,000 medallion for the leader and a ₱20 million development grant for their LGU or organisation, restricted to development projects; and a ₱500 million endowment fund held by the Bangsamoro Treasury Office and invested under Islamic financing principles, from whose profits alone the awards are paid.
